implemented_requirements.evidence: LEVELS = {"Beginner": (9, 9, 10), "Intermediate": (16, 16, 40), "Expert": (30, 16, 99)} and menu buttons created for each level.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Player uncovers cells by clicking on them
implemented_requirements.evidence: Each board button is created with command=lambda r=r, c=c: self.reveal(r, c) which is invoked on left‑click.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Numbers on uncovered cells indicate how many mines are adjacent
implemented_requirements.evidence: Cell.adj is computed in place_mines; paint() sets button text to str(cell.adj) when adj > 0.

implemented_requirements.requirement: If a mine is uncovered, the player loses
implemented_requirements.evidence: reveal() calls game_over(r, c) when cell.mine is True; game_over() marks the board as over and shows mines.

implemented_requirements.requirement: The game displays the board with updated markings after each move
implemented_requirements.evidence: paint() updates button appearance for each revealed cell; toggle_flag() updates flag visuals; tick() updates timer label.
Button bind "<Button-3>" calls toggle_flag(r, c); flag state stored in Cell.flagged and visualized.
When flagged, button text is set to "\u2691" with background "#ffb347" and foreground "#b00000".

critical_issues: Right‑click flagging uses "<Button-3>", which may not work on macOS without additional handling (e.g., <Control-Button-1>).
Flag counter can become negative if the player places more flags than mines, but this does not affect core gameplay.
judge.summary: The provided main.py implements a fully functional classic Minesweeper with three difficulty levels, left‑click reveal, numbered adjacency hints, loss on mine, win detection, a right‑click flagging system, and distinct flag visuals. The GUI updates after each move and includes a timer and mine counter. The code appears syntactically correct and runnable with Python's standard Tkinter library, so it meets all core requirements. Minor platform‑specific flagging concerns are noted but do not prevent the core functionality.
